findings.title: traceID field dropped from "Plugin Request Completed" log lines
findings.body: Before this change, LoggerMiddleware explicitly appended a "traceID" field to every "Plugin Request Completed" log line via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). This PR removes that code (and the tracing import) and relies entirely on contextual attributes attached by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware — but instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname; it never adds traceID. Nothing else in the plugin client middleware chain attaches traceID via log.WithContextualAttributes, so these log lines lose the trace ID whenever an upstream HTTP middleware hasn't already put it into the context — e.g. plugin calls originating from background services such as alerting evaluations, where the trace exists only as a span in ctx. This breaks log-to-trace correlation that previously always worked. Fix by either keeping the explicit traceID param in LoggerMiddleware or adding traceID inside instrumentContext.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh instance, so logs via FromContext are never recorded
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(). This matters because the production code changed in this PR (LoggerMiddleware) now logs exclusively through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). Any test that injects a *TestLogger and then asserts on InfoLogs/ErrorLogs/etc. of the instance it holds will see zero recorded calls — tests expecting a log will fail confusingly, and tests asserting that nothing was logged will silently false-pass even though the code under test did log. The fake should return f (or record into shared state) so that logs written through FromContext are observable by the test.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier in the chain
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware previously built the pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, and dsUID log fields itself from req.PluginContext, so it was self-contained. After this change those fields only appear if ContextualLoggerMiddleware ran earlier in the middleware stack and attached them as contextual attributes. The production wiring in CreateMiddlewares happens to order them correctly, but NewLoggerMiddleware is exported and can be composed into other middleware stacks (tests, other decorator constructions); in any stack without ContextualLoggerMiddleware ahead of it, the "Plugin Request Completed" lines lose all plugin-identifying fields with no error or warning. At minimum the ordering requirement should be documented on NewLoggerMiddleware (the old InstrumentationMiddleware had such a comment, and it was removed in the rename).

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test, and no test covers the moved log fields
findings.body: The PR adds a new middleware (ContextualLoggerMiddleware) responsible for attaching endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname to the request context, but adds no test verifying those attributes are attached, and the renamed metrics_middleware_test.go only covers the prometheus metrics. There is also no test asserting that LoggerMiddleware's "Plugin Request Completed" output still contains the fields that were moved out of it — which is exactly why the traceID regression introduced by this PR (the explicit traceID field was removed and is no longer added anywhere in the chain) is not caught by the test suite. A small test chaining ContextualLoggerMiddleware + LoggerMiddleware and asserting the resulting log fields would lock in the intended behavior.
